{{short description|American microbiologist}}
'''Joan Bray Rose''' (born March 5, 1954) is an American microbiologist.

Rose earned her bachelor's degree in microbiology from the [[University of Arizona]], followed by a master's degree in the same subject from the [[University of Wyoming]]. She returned to Arizona to obtain a doctorate, also in microbiology. Rose then taught at the [[University of South Florida]] until 2003.<ref>{{cite news |title=Joan Bray Rose |url=https://msu.edu/honoredfaculty/directory/rose-bray-joan.html |access-date=January 28, 2019 |publisher=Michigan State University}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Joan Rose: Biography |url=http://www.iwa-network.org/people/joan-rose/ |publisher=International Water Association}}</ref> She serves as the Homer Nowlin Chair in Water Research at [[Michigan State University]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Rose, Joan B. |url=https://mmg.natsci.msu.edu/people/faculty/rose-joan-b/ |publisher=Michigan State University |access-date=2019-01-27 |archive-date=2019-02-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190220011536/https://mmg.natsci.msu.edu/people/faculty/rose-joan-b/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Rose won the [[Athalie Richardson Irvine Clarke Prize]] in 2001, and used some of the prize money to endow the Rose Water Fellowship at Michigan State University.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kastl |first1=Mackenzie |last2=Salk |first2=Kateri |last3=Rose |first3=Joan |title=Rose Water Fellowship awardee named |url=https://msutoday.msu.edu/news/2015/rose-water-fellowship-awardee-named/ |access-date=January 28, 2019 |publisher=Michigan State University |date=June 17, 2015}}</ref> She was the 2008 recipient of the [[International Water Association]]'s Hei-jin Woo Award.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dr. Joan Rose wins IWA award |url=https://www.estormwater.com/dr-joan-rose-wins-iwa-award |access-date=January 28, 2019 |publisher=Storm Water Solutions |date=September 10, 2008}}</ref> Rose was elected a member of the [[United States National Academy of Engineering]] in 2011 "for contributions to improving water quality safety and public health."<ref>{{cite news |title=Dr. Joan B. Rose |url=https://www.nae.edu/MembersSection/Directory20412/42022.aspx |access-date=January 28, 2019 |publisher=United States National Academy of Engineering}}</ref> In 2015, the government of Singapore granted Rose [[Honorary Citizen of Singapore|honorary citizenship]] to honor her research on the nation's water infrastructure and quality.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ward |first1=Kim |title=MSU professor named honorary citizen of Singapore |url=https://msutoday.msu.edu/news/2015/msu-professor-named-honorary-citizen-of-singapore-1/ |access-date=January 28, 2019 |publisher=Michigan State University |date=October 21, 2015}}</ref> The next year, Rose was awarded the [[Stockholm Water Prize]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ward |first1=Kim |title=MSU global water scientist awarded world's top water prize |url=https://msutoday.msu.edu/news/2016/msu-global-water-scientist-awarded-worlds-top-water-prize/ |access-date=January 28, 2019 |publisher=Michigan State University |date=March 22, 2016}}</ref>
